subject: Day 62: plan a Botanical Garden loop
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 62 closes out week nine, the calm post-vaccine stretch. A low-stimulation outdoor outing fits the moment: it gives Avi varied sensory input and the parents daylight and movement without overloading him.

Action items
- Plan a quiet stroller loop through the SF Botanical Garden for a weekday this week, mid-morning before crowds, packing a sun hat and one feed's worth of milk; greenery and dappled light are exactly the low-key sensory variety he can handle now.
- Keep vitamin D supplementation at 400 IU per day for breastfed or predominantly breastfed infants regardless of how much outdoor time he gets; sun exposure does not replace the supplement at this age. AAP vitamin D: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/healthy-living/nutrition/Pages/Vitamin-D-On-the-Double.aspx
- Lock the 4-month visit on the calendar, window day 112-126, for RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, and IPV #2. AAP immunization policy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/immunizations/aap-policy-on-immunizations/

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Brief fussing when the stroller stops moving, and squinting in bright light; shade the canopy and keep moving.
- [monitor] Spit-up that is forceful or paired with arching during feeds rather than the usual easy posset; document frequency for the next visit.
- [call within 24h] A clear drop in wet diapers over a day, or a new murmur noted by anyone examining him.
- [call now] Rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher under 90 days, blue lips, or labored breathing means call now, and 911 for blue lips.

Enrichment opportunities
- Plan a calm stroller loop through the SF Botanical Garden for greenery, fresh air, and gentle sensory variety, keeping the outing short and the canopy shaded.
- Let him track leaves and dappled light moving overhead, recline the stroller slightly so the moving pattern fills his visual field and feeds smooth tracking. AAP baby senses: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/default.aspx
- Hum a calm tune as you walk the paths, pairing your live voice with the new setting; participatory singing, not recorded background, is what carries the benefit. Trainor infant music study: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22490184/

Upcoming
- Day 57-72 (now): final days of the post-vaccine window; mild lingering fussiness still counts as low concern.
- Day 84-91: sleep-consolidation window opens; begin a consistent dim-after-sunset routine.
- Day 112-126: 4-month well visit, with RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, and IPV #2.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Smiles on his own to get your attention
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Initiates the smile rather than responding to yours — emerging social agency.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/smiles-to-get-attention/complete

- Chuckles (not yet a full laugh)
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Throaty soft laugh sounds. Precedes the full belly laugh by a few weeks.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/chuckles/complete

- Turns head toward the sound of your voice
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Localizes sound source. Worth raising with the pediatrician if absent at the 4-month visit.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/turns-head-toward-sound/complete

- Makes sounds back when you talk to him
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Conversational turn-taking. Foundation for later vocabulary growth.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/makes-sounds-back/complete

- Opens mouth when she sees the breast or bottle
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Anticipatory recognition — feeding is now associated with the sight, not just the sensation.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/opens-mouth-for-breast/complete
